# Spiritual Translation

**¶7:** It is fitting that this be understood inwardly. The external truths called "the great truth" are the five faculties of interior understanding that complete and perfect the external form of the ascending order of Divine Wisdom — the fully regenerate human. These faculties were purified and made whole through the influx of divine mediation into the mind.

**¶8:** In contrast, those called "fragments": the fragments are the scattered and consumed portion of wisdom. This wisdom is compounded and entangled throughout the whole external order of the mind, within the dominant persuasions that rule from above, which persist across all the general doctrinal frameworks of thought. Moreover, its radiance is that appearance of truth which shines forth and manifests in the particular knowledges bound in sequence and in the active forces of orderly spiritual progression. And likewise, those fragments of wisdom entangled in the three degrees of the natural mind below, above the sustaining foundation [GAP-1] upon the natural plane that lies beneath the sustaining foundation. These are called "fragments" because [GAP-2] established [GAP-3]

**¶9:** However, the "great external truths that have been worn away and torn apart," which we have declared, refer to this entangled living spiritual force. It is harvested, severed, and consumed. It is overpowered by the five provinces of the selfhood — the proprium — which creep insidiously as they shift from state to state within the mind.

**¶10:** On the other hand, [GAP-4: REVIEW these] we have called "the representations and the greatly degraded external truths" [GAP-5] are the three encompassing external truths belonging to thought, to love, and to truth itself. These the Divine Life clothed upon its own external form. With them it established order throughout the whole created mind. With them also it emptied the containing forms of their corrupt contents. It swept them clean and laid them bare before the sustaining foundation at the basis of all states.

**¶11:** Conversely, "the fundamental spiritual substances" — we have given them this designation — are that living force which persists within all things of the natural mind. It rises through the generative interiors of every degree of the natural plane, collecting itself together, and flowing forth upon all states of life.

**¶12:** And then, the "[GAP-6: REVIEW Wisdom] bound in suffering" — [GAP-7: REVIEW we have designated] this captive "wisdom held in bondage." It [GAP-8] all [GAP-9] upon the natural mind, both where truth is absent and where truth is present.

**¶13:** Also, that which is called the "counsel of life" is the divine calling and the responsive obedience to it. It moves within all those spiritual forces we have named. It awakens them from dormancy, grants them rest and peace, and impels them toward their proper spiritual activity.

**¶14:** That which is called "the spiritual life that is slain" — which is killed, oppressed, and destroyed — is the living power within works, natural goods, and interior truths. These shall be violently separated, torn away, and cut down; and they provide sustenance to the provinces of selfhood. Further: should natural good be deprived of truth, and should an external truth become fragmented, it will perish. Again, this is a portion of that entire spiritual life which is slain and destroyed; since even this whole portion of it they kill [GAP-10]

**¶15:** For all these designations [GAP-11] are a single [GAP-12] since the beginning, it [GAP-13] as it communicates wisdom; but they were separated into all these distinct forms during the primordial contest between good and evil. They became fixed in all these altered appearances and these many identities. Yet if now all these varieties are laid bare, and stripped of every outward appearance, and parted from every separate name — they will gather together into a single divine form, and a single divine identity, unalterable and unchangeable forever in the state of their original essence, from which they were sent forth to confront the onslaught of evil and falsity.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: “It is proper for you to understand this. The garments that are named ‘great garment’ are the five intellectuals that make perfect the body of the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man. They were purified by the coming of the Ambassador.

“In contrast, the ones named ‘rag’: the rags are the devoured enlightening power. It is compounded and entangled in the body of the universe in the rulers who are above, who exist in all the firmaments. Also, its shine is that which lights up and is displayed in the stars of the chain and the powers of the course. And likewise, these rags that are entangled in these three earths below, above the head of the Porter [and upon the Porter, and also] on the earth that is under the Porter. These are named the ‘rags’, because [they are] set [apart in all things]

“However, the ‘great worn and torn apart garments’, which we have proclaimed, is this entangled living power. It is reaped, cut, and devoured. It is overpowered by the five worlds of the flesh, which creep as they move from place to place.

“On the other hand, [these] we have termed the ‘images and the great tattered clothes’ [they] are the three great garments of the wind, the fire, and the water. These the Living Spirit cloaked upon his body. With them he set in order things in the universe. With them also he emptied the vessels. He swept them out and laid them bare in front of the Porter at the foundation of all things.

“Conversely, ‘[the ele]ments’, we have called them this name, are this power that remains in all things below. It rises up in the wombs of all the earths, gathering together, and pouring forth upon all things.
“And then, the ‘[Light] Cross’ [we have termed] this bound ‘light power’. It [is mingled in] all [things] upon the earth, in the dry and the moist.
“Also, the one named the ‘counsel of life’ is the summons and the obedience. It moves in all these powers that we have named. It awakens them, gives them ease, and drives them to their movement.

“The one named ‘the soul that is slain’, which is killed, oppressed and murdered; it is this power of fruit, vegetables and seeds. They shall be threshed, plucked and cut down; and they give nourishment to the worlds of the flesh. Further: the wood should it be dry, and the garment should it become ragged, will perish. Again, it is [a pa]rt of this entire soul that is slain and killed; since also even this whole part of it they kill [and devour]

“For all these names [that we have spoken] are a single [power] since the beginning, it [was one] as it enlightens; but they separated into all these parts in this first contest. They became set in all these altered forms, and these many names. Of course, if now all these varieties are laid bare, and stripped of all these appearances, and parted from all these names; they will gather together and make a single form, and a single name, unaltered and unchangeable for ever in the land of their first essence, from which they were sent forth against the enemy.”

fills.explanation: Three earths are specified: (1) above the Porter's head, (2) upon the Porter himself, and (3) under the Porter — the gap must name the middle of these three locations to satisfy the "three earths below" just mentioned.

The sentence requires a subject and copula to explain why these fragments are called "rags": "because they are set apart" — matching the chapter's pattern of passive descriptions of the scattered light.

The reason they are called "rags" (fragments) is that the enlightening power has been set apart — scattered and fragmented — throughout all things in the cosmos, just as rags are pieces torn from a whole garment.
The editor's "these" fits perfectly as a demonstrative pronoun opening the naming formula, matching the chapter's consistent pattern of "these/the ones [we have termed/named] X are Y."

A resumptive pronoun is needed to bridge the naming clause ("these we have termed X") and the identification clause ("are the three great garments"), following the standard Kephalaia definitional pattern.

The "Light Cross" (crux luminis) is the standard Manichaean designation for the suffering light bound in all of nature; "Light" is the established natural-plane term corresponding to the spiritual sense of "Wisdom held in bondage."
The editor's "we have termed" fits the chapter's naming formula used in ¶10 and ¶11, where each designation is introduced with a first-person-plural verb of naming.

The Light Cross represents light that is mixed and bound throughout all of nature; "mingled" is the standard Manichaean verb for how the captive light subsists within matter, fitting the spiritual sense of wisdom pervading the natural mind.

Completing "all things upon the earth" — the standard Kephalaia formula for the totality of the natural order, further specified by "in the dry and the moist" (i.e., all conditions of material existence).

The chapter consistently pairs killing with devouring/consuming when describing what the powers of the flesh do to the living light (cf. ¶8 "devoured enlightening power," ¶9 "reaped, cut, and devoured"), completing the sentence's logic about total destruction of the soul that is slain.

The summary paragraph requires a relative clause identifying the names previously enumerated; "that we have spoken" is a standard Kephalaia summary formula, complementing the chapter's use of "proclaimed," "termed," and "called" in individual paragraphs.

The chapter's entire argument is that all the names refer to one underlying reality, consistently called "power" throughout: "enlightening power" (¶8), "living power" (¶9, ¶11), "light power" (¶12), "power" (¶13) — the single divine substance that was fragmented.

The passage contrasts original unity ("a single power... it was one") with subsequent fragmentation ("they separated into all these parts"), directly mirroring the chapter's theme that the one light was whole before the primordial contest divided it into many forms and names.
